feedback: Written before this candidate has raced; no result is stated for it. Evidence: iterations 1, 4 and 6 used the same geometry and controller and each scored 69.3241, so this geometry is reproducible. Iteration 3 (y = 0.03 m, same controller as iteration 1) scored 59.64, so keep y = 0.05 m. Iteration 2 (16 mm footprint, same controller) scored 54.45, so keep 12 mm. Iteration 5 (span ±0.04 m, same controller) scored 52.47 and did not bring line loss clearly below 1 per run, so keep ±0.03 m. Line loss has stayed at about 1 per run through iterations 0 to 6, and steering oscillation (0.07 to 0.15) is not the limiting factor. The geometry is therefore not the open question. The Integrator is testing a slower base_speed (1.15) with the geometry held, so you do not need to change anything this round. Body width does not move the off-track limit, max(0.06, 0.0125 + body_width/4) = 0.06 m across your range, so do not treat it as a lever.
requested_changes: Hold the iteration 1 geometry unchanged: five 12 mm sensors at x = -0.03, -0.015, 0, 0.015, 0.03 m, y = 0.05 m, with the wheel, body and mass values as they are. Iterations 1, 4 and 6 show this scores 69.3241.

If the next race shows line_loss_events clearly below 1 per run with the Integrator's slower base_speed, you may keep this geometry and test a single later geometry change. If line loss is unchanged, keep the geometry and let the Integrator work on controller line-loss handling.
Do not move the forward offset (y = 0.03 m cost about 10 points in iteration 3) or the footprint (16 mm cost about 15 points in iteration 2) without a clear controller explanation.
